stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Folklorists who collect the same story in different places expect it to drift, but Mara Quill's 1968 survey of Ozark storytellers found that one widely told tale shifted in only a single respect as it moved from county to county. ______ the trickster at its center was a fox in Stone County, a crow in neighboring Taney County, and a raccoon farther east.
explanation: The first sentence says the tale changed in 'only a single respect' but doesn't say what that respect was. The second sentence names it: the trickster's species. Nothing is being picked from a larger set. The same claim is just stated more exactly, and that's what 'Specifically' signals.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. You saw a broad sentence followed by a detail and reached for 'for example.' But the passage says the tale shifted in only one respect, so there are no other changes this could be an example of. The second sentence spells out that one change; it isn't one sample from a group.

C.why: 'Nevertheless' signals that the second sentence goes against the first. Here it supports the first sentence by showing what the single change was. You may have taken the surprising variety of animals for a contradiction.

D.why: 'Afterward' marks a later event. The animal versions aren't something that happened after Quill's finding; they are the finding. You read a time sequence into a sentence that only adds detail.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Astronomers rarely see an exoplanet directly; instead, they rely on at least four indirect signs that a star has an unseen companion. ______ a planet crossing in front of its star blocks a sliver of the starlight, producing a small, regular dip in brightness that telescopes can record.
explanation: The first sentence names a category of 'at least four indirect signs.' The second describes one of them, the dip in brightness when a planet passes in front of its star. A sentence that gives one member of a larger group calls for 'For instance.'

B.why: This is the reverse of the subtype's trap. 'Specifically' would mean the second sentence spells out the whole of the first claim. But the first sentence promises at least four signs and the second gives only one. When one member is picked from a counted group, that's an example, not a specification.

C.why: 'In other words' introduces a restatement. The second sentence doesn't rephrase the idea of indirect signs. It adds new, narrower information about one particular sign. You took added detail for rewording.

D.why: 'Even so' signals a point made in spite of the one before it. The transit method supports the claim that astronomers use indirect signs, so nothing needs to be overcome.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: During the 2010s, many endurance coaches overhauled one part of their programs: the way they judged whether an athlete had recovered from hard training. ______ instead of asking runners how rested they felt, coaches began measuring each athlete's heart-rate variability every morning and adjusting the day's workload to match the reading.
explanation: The first sentence names one change in general terms: coaches overhauled how they judged recovery. The second says exactly what that change was, moving from self-reports to morning heart-rate readings. Since it spells out that same single change in sharper, more informative terms, 'Specifically' is correct.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. 'Many coaches' sounds like a group, but the claim is about one overhauled part of their programs. The second sentence describes that one overhaul in detail; it doesn't pick one case out of several. 'For example' implies a set that isn't there.

B.why: 'In other words' would mean the second sentence only rephrases the first. Instead, it adds new information the first sentence never gave: heart-rate variability, daily measurement, and workloads adjusted to the reading. You took narrowing with new detail for simple rewording.

D.why: 'Similarly' introduces a separate, parallel case. The second sentence isn't another change like the first; it is the first change, described in detail. You read an addition where there's a zoom-in.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: A meal's iron content says little about how much iron the body actually takes in, because several substances commonly eaten alongside iron-rich foods interfere with its absorption. ______ the tannins in black tea bind to iron in the gut, so a cup of tea with lunch can sharply reduce the iron absorbed from that meal. Calcium and certain fibers have a similar effect.
explanation: The first sentence mentions 'several substances' that block iron absorption. The second sentence picks one of them, tea tannins, and the last sentence confirms there are others (calcium and fibers). One member taken from a larger group is an example, so 'For instance' is correct.

A.why: This is the reverse of the subtype's trap. 'Specifically' would mean the tannin sentence spells out the whole of 'several substances.' The passage then names calcium and fibers as further members, which shows the tannin sentence describes just one of them. That makes it an example.

C.why: 'As a result' would make the tea's effect a consequence of the first sentence. But the fact that several substances interfere with iron doesn't cause tannins to bind iron. The tannins are one case of that fact. You read cause and effect into a general-to-instance relationship.

D.why: 'By contrast' signals that the second sentence differs from the first. Tea tannins blocking iron agrees with the claim that some foods interfere with absorption. Nothing is being contrasted.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Vaccination clinics drew most of the headlines, but between 2015 and 2022 the Harlow County health department also took one quieter step that researchers now credit with reducing childhood illness. ______ it paid to replace the lead service pipes in more than 4,000 older homes, and blood-lead levels among local children fell by nearly a third.
explanation: The first sentence refers to 'one quieter step' without saying what it was. The second identifies it: replacing lead service pipes. It names the single step the first sentence pointed to, so 'Specifically' is correct.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. The first sentence describes one step, not a group of steps, so the pipe replacement can't be one example among several. It is the step itself, spelled out.

B.why: The word 'also' in the first sentence pulls you toward an addition word. But the pipe replacement isn't a second step added to the quieter step. It's the same step, named. 'Additionally' would make one action look like two.

C.why: 'Meanwhile' signals something happening at the same time as another event. The second sentence doesn't describe a separate event running alongside the first; it says what the first one was. You read a time relationship into a specifying one.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: In a twelve-week feeding trial, nutrition researcher Ama Owusu-Ansah changed just one element of the standard lunch served to 400 students at a secondary school in Kumasi, Ghana. ______ she replaced the polished white rice with a parboiled variety whose starch the body digests more slowly. By the end of the trial, the students' afternoon blood glucose readings had become noticeably steadier, and teachers reported fewer complaints of drowsiness after lunch.
explanation: The first sentence says Owusu-Ansah changed one element of the lunch but doesn't say which one. The next sentence names it exactly: the white rice became parboiled rice. Nothing is being picked out of a larger group. The sentence just spells out the same single change more precisely, so 'Specifically' is the right transition.

A.why: You saw a general sentence followed by a detail and reached for 'for example.' But the passage says only one element changed, so there's no group of changes to take a sample from. The rice swap is the whole change, not one instance of it.

C.why: 'Nevertheless' signals that the second sentence goes against the first. Replacing the rice doesn't contradict changing one element of the lunch. It is that change.

D.why: 'Similarly' means the second sentence describes a separate thing that parallels the first. The rice swap isn't a second, similar change. It's the one change the first sentence already mentioned.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Shape-memory alloys, metals that return to a preset form when they are heated, have found work in a surprisingly wide range of fields since they were first developed. ______ orthodontists use nickel-titanium wires that warm to body temperature inside the mouth and slowly pull crooked teeth into line. Aerospace engineers, meanwhile, have tested alloy strips that reshape the exhaust nozzles of jet engines to reduce noise during takeoff.
explanation: The first sentence names a category: a 'wide range of fields.' The next sentence gives one member of that category, orthodontics, and the sentence after it ('meanwhile') adds another, aerospace. A single case taken from a larger group calls for 'For example.'

A.why: 'Instead' means one option is replacing another. The orthodontic wires don't replace anything in the first sentence. They're one of the fields that sentence describes.

B.why: This is the reverse trap. 'In other words' would mean the second sentence restates the first. It doesn't. It adds new and much narrower information about one field, and another field follows right after, so it's an example, not a rephrasing.

C.why: 'Even so' sets up a concession or contrast. The use in orthodontics supports the claim about many fields. It doesn't push against it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Over a four-year project, the river district of the small industrial town of Kesselbrück underwent a transformation that few of its residents had believed possible. ______ engineers demolished the elevated highway that had covered the Kessel River for half a century and rebuilt the exposed channel as a two-kilometer park with stepped stone banks. Property values along the corridor rose by nearly a third within five years of the park's opening.
explanation: The first sentence mentions a single event, 'a transformation,' in vague terms. The next sentence says exactly what that transformation was: removing the highway and rebuilding the channel as a park. It restates the same event in precise terms instead of picking one case from a set, so 'Specifically' fits.

A.why: 'Afterward' puts the demolition after the transformation. But the demolition and rebuilding are the transformation, not a later step.

B.why: This is the subtype's trap. The first sentence names one transformation, not a group of them, so there's nothing to sample from. When the following sentence just spells out a single event in detail, the transition is 'specifically,' not 'for example.'

D.why: 'Regardless' means the second sentence holds true despite the first. The engineering work doesn't happen in spite of the transformation. It is the transformation.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Ecologists monitoring Lake Tanvik have documented several ways in which the invasive zebra mussel has reshaped the lake's food web since it arrived in the 1990s. ______ by filtering plankton out of the water, the mussels have left far less food for the young perch that once depended on it. The clearer water has also allowed sunlight to reach the lakebed, where dense mats of algae now grow in places that were once bare.
explanation: The first sentence names a plural category: 'several ways' the mussel has reshaped the food web. The next sentence gives one of those ways, the loss of plankton for young perch, and the following sentence adds a second with 'also.' Because the sentence describes one member of a larger set, 'For example' is correct.

B.why: 'Specifically' would mean the plankton effect is the full, precise version of the 'several ways.' It isn't. It's only one of them, and the passage goes on to describe another ('also'). The word 'several' tells you an example is coming, not a restatement.

C.why: 'Still' signals a contrast or concession. The plankton effect supports the claim that the mussels reshaped the food web. It doesn't qualify or push against it.

D.why: 'Consequently' would mean the mussels filter plankton because ecologists documented their effects. The filtering is one of the documented effects, not a result of the documenting.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: When linguist Ines Marrow began recording older residents of the North Sea island of Hesk, she found that their speech differed from mainland speech in only one consistent respect. ______ islanders dropped the 'r' sound whenever it ended a syllable, so that 'harbor' was pronounced closer to 'hah-bah.' Marrow suspects the pattern arrived with sailors from eastern England during the island's fishing boom in the 1800s.
explanation: The first sentence says the island's speech differed from the mainland's 'in only one consistent respect' but doesn't name it. The next sentence tells you exactly what that one respect was. There's no set of differences to choose from, since the passage says there was only one. The sentence is zooming in on that single difference, so 'Specifically' is correct.

A.why: This is the subtype's trap. 'For instance' would mean the dropped 'r' is one of several differences. The passage says there was only one, so the sentence spells it out in detail and isn't an example.

B.why: The passage is about island speech differing from mainland speech, and that may have made a contrast word seem right. But the transition has to connect the two sentences, and the second agrees with the first by naming the difference it mentioned. Nothing between the sentences is contradicted.

C.why: 'Later' makes the second sentence a step that comes after the first in time. The dropped 'r' isn't a later discovery. It's the same difference Marrow found, described more precisely.
